input.summary:
Implemented the full Task Management API with the following files:

**src/event-bus.ts** — In-memory pub/sub `EventBus` with `publish(event, payload)` and `subscribe(event, callback)`. Isolates all inter-service communication.

**src/services/user-service.ts** — CRUD for `{ id, name, email }` backed by a private `Map`. No external dependencies.

**src/services/project-service.ts** — CRUD + `addMember`/`removeMember` for `{ id, name, description, memberIds[] }`.

**src/services/task-service.ts** — CRUD + `assign` + `changeStatus` + `getByProject` for `{ id, title, description, status, assigneeId, projectId }`. Enforces forward-only `todo → in-progress → done` transitions. Publishes `task.assigned` and `task.statusChanged` events via the EventBus.

**src/services/comment-service.ts** — create/getById/getByTask/delete for `{ id, taskId, authorId, body, createdAt }`. Publishes `comment.added` events. Accepts `taskTitle`, `authorName`, and `assigneeId` as resolved parameters (supplied by the router) so it never calls other services directly.

**src/services/notification-service.ts** — Subscribes to `task.assigned`, `task.statusChanged`, and `comment.added` events in its constructor. Creates `{ id, userId, message, read, createdAt }` notifications automatically. Exposes `getByUser` and `markAsRead`.

**src/router.ts** — Pure Node.js `http`-based router (no frameworks). Parses path segments and query params, delegates to services, returns JSON. Resolves cross-service data (task title, user name, assignee) at the router boundary before passing it to services — preserving the no-direct-service-calls constraint while still producing rich event payloads.

**src/main.ts** — Wires everything together: creates the EventBus, instantiates all services, builds the handler via `createRouter`, and starts the HTTP server on port 3000 (or `$PORT`).

**src/demo.ts** — End-to-end demo: creates users → project → adds/removes members → creates tasks → assigns tasks → changes status (including invalid backward-transition test) → adds comments → checks notifications → marks notifications read → single-resource lookups → updates → 404 tests → deletes. All 40+ assertions pass.
